claims.text: The target nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and initially form a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
Increasing the atomic-radius mismatch among constituent elements increases lattice distortion.
A higher mixing-enthalpy penalty contributes to greater lattice distortion.
Greater lattice distortion raises the activation-energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
Lattice distortion and multielement mixing reduce atomic diffusivity in multimetal nanoparticles.
Sluggish atomic diffusion inhibits phase separation and elemental segregation.
Configurational entropy from multielement mixing favors and stabilizes a homogeneous solid-solution phase.
Thermally activated diffusion across 473–1923 K drives elemental segregation and chemical ordering.
The competition between entropy-driven mixing and diffusion kinetics governs structural and chemical stability.
Nanoparticles with greater lattice distortion will retain a homogeneous single phase to higher temperatures than the baseline nanoparticles.
The enhanced-distortion nanoparticles will exhibit a delayed emergence of secondary phases or other XRD changes.
Elemental mapping will show less segregation in the enhanced-distortion nanoparticles than in the baseline nanoparticles.
The baseline composition with lower lattice distortion will segregate or chemically order at a lower temperature.
Reactive atmospheres or extrinsic kinetic effects may change the predicted relationship between lattice distortion and stability.
The comparison will use an inert atmosphere, a 473–1923 K temperature ramp, and otherwise identical synthesis and testing procedures.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant delay in segregation, improved elemental homogeneity, or slower diffusion in the modified nanoparticles would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that lattice distortion is the only variable, but replacing an element necessarily changes chemical identity and, by design, also changes mixing enthalpy. The comparison therefore does not isolate lattice distortion alone.
